bull_bear.body: Highly confident, upbeat, and execution-focused; merger approval treated as a catalyst for transformation; synergy realization timeline (12-18 months) clearly articulated; strong emphasis on R&D and manufacturing integration; no hedging on guidance, projecting 20%+ margins as baseline
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Viyash’s CDMO pipeline (15+ products >$1B market value) is a hidden asset — revenue and margin inflection likely from FY28, not FY27; SeQuent’s API growth was held back by customer timing, not demand — visibility improves from Q4FY26; 7 backward-integrated products (formulation → API) are margin accretive and reduce third-party dependency
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Deleveraging is the headline balance-sheet message: Net Debt to LTM EBITDA (EBITDA adjusted for ESOP) at 0.1x versus 0.2x in Q4 FY26, with the chart series running 1.4x in Q1'25 down to 0.1x in Q1'27.
- The deck contradicts itself on the net debt amount on the same snapshot slide — it shows both "Net Debt - ₹ 1,661" and "Net Debt- ₹ 861 Mn"; both readings are reported as printed, not reconciled.
- Lower leverage is being converted into P&L relief: "Finance Cost reduction on account of the reduction in debt".
- Equity-linked compensation stepped up structurally: "ESOP cost increase on account of incremental ESOP grants pursuant to the scheme of amalgamation".
- No dividend, buyback or payout policy is mentioned anywhere in the deck.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Integrated platform across API, advanced intermediates, human health formulations, animal health formulations and CDMO, enabling backward integration and cost optimisation
- >85% backward integration across key products, strengthening supply security and margin resilience
- Broad global regulatory footprint with 10 USFDA-approved manufacturing sites among 16 manufacturing facilities and approvals from USFDA, EU GMP, WHO GMP, PMDA, TGA, COFEPRIS and ANVISA
- "One R&D" platform of 250+ scientists including 20+ PhDs, with 175+ patents filed and 55+ granted, supporting complex chemistry including cytotoxic and high-potency APIs
- Multi-geography commercial presence (150+ countries) and manufacturing/subsidiary footprint across Spain, Turkey, Brazil, Benelux, USA and India providing local market access
- Diversified customer base across large generic manufacturers, innovator/proprietary brands and global animal health companies
- Credit rating upgraded (long-term IND A to IND AA-, short-term IND A1 to IND A1+) reflecting strengthened balance sheet with low net debt/EBITDA
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regulatory risk — Operations across multiple jurisdictions are subject to evolving pharmaceutical regulatory requirements; the Company relies on compliance frameworks and regular training to keep pace with changing rules.
- Environment, Health and Safety (EHS) risk — Manufacturing complex/high-potency APIs and formulations carries EHS exposure; mitigated through stringent environmental, health and safety standards and continuous monitoring across operations.
- Currency volatility risk — Multi-geography manufacturing and sales (India, Spain, Turkey, Brazil, USA and others) expose the Company to foreign-exchange fluctuations, managed via natural hedging and monitoring mechanisms.
- Interest rate risk — Borrowings carry a mix of fixed and floating rates, exposing the Company to interest-cost fluctuations even as it manages this through structured debt composition.
- Credit risk — Exposure to counterparty non-payment across a global customer base is managed through disciplined credit evaluation, receivables monitoring and delegation of authority.
- Liquidity risk — Global operations and working-capital needs require a prudent liquidity framework backed by efficient cash-flow management and access to adequate funding sources.
- Information technology and cybersecurity risk — Scaling operations across geographies increases exposure to IT/cybersecurity threats, addressed through continued investment in IT infrastructure and cybersecurity frameworks.
- Market risk — Macroeconomic developments, pricing trends and geopolitical factors can disrupt business; the Company monitors these to enable responsive decision-making.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: Formulations: INR3,351cr (+18% YoY), led by Europe (+14%), emerging markets (+27%), India (+6%); API: INR830cr (+7% YoY), with new U.S. launch and FDA audit clearance; Viyash API/Intermediates: ~65-70% of its INR428cr revenue; CDMO: 15+ products >$1B market value, launches from FY28; Companion Animal: 4 new products developed, pipeline accelerating
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- Self-described as "an integrated pharmaceutical platform across animal and human health backed by science and IP", combining API & CDMO, human formulations and animal formulations (companion plus farm animals).
- Global presence claimed at "150+ Countries" and "250+ global customers", supported by "1,000+ Registrations".
- Positions itself as IP and technology driven: "250+ Scientists" and "175+ Patents Filed" (the milestone slide instead says R&D was "expanded to over 200 scientists").
- The current entity is the product of the SeQuent Scientific / Viyash Life Sciences combination — the milestone slide labels 2025 onwards as "Integration & Global Reach" with "Unified manufacturing operations", and the MD's note credits "the continued success of our integration efforts and the strength of the combined entity".
- Management is presented as "Industry leaders with 30+ years experience".
business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Bio For Life (Italy) — rationale given as access to a large companion animal market in Italy, a companion animal portfolio of 85-90 products extendable to other core markets, a platform to "Launch our global pipeline in Italy" via a salesforce with "85% vet clinic coverage in Italy", and "Strong talent addition in Italy"; the MD frames it as "market access and a platform to launch our product portfolio in key European markets".
- [Corporate action] The company is "Formerly known as Sequent Scientific Limited"; the scheme of amalgamation is referenced as the source of incremental ESOP grants, and the forward-looking-statement disclaimer at the back still reads "SeQuent Scientific Ltd."
- [History] Milestones cite acquisition of Mylan's API and formulation units in Vizag and Mumbai, a strategic investment by the Carlyle Group, and acquisitions of Symed Labs and Appco Pharma LLC; Viyash Life Sciences itself was founded in February 2019 by Dr Haribabu Bodepudi and expanded via Vindhya Pharma and Vandana Life Sciences.
- [Brand] Alivira is the dedicated animal health brand established in the 2014-2019 phase, with USFDA veterinary API approvals cited.
- [Governance] Board listed as Dr. Kamal Sharma (Chairman, Independent), Mr. Milind Sarwate and Ms. Revati Kasture (Independent), Mr. Anuj Poddar, Mr. Amit Jain and Mr. Abhiroop Jayanthi (Non-executive), Dr. Haribabu Bodepudi (Managing Director and Group CEO), Mr. Rajaram Narayanan (Executive Director and CEO - Animal Health) and Mr. Srinivas Vasireddy (Executive Director).
business.title: Notable from the deck

business.body: Viyash Scientific Limited, formed through the integration of Viyash Lifesciences Private Limited and erstwhile SeQuent Scientific Limited, manufactures Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (APIs), advanced intermediates and finished formulations for both human and animal health, sold to large generic manufacturers, innovator/proprietary brands and global animal health companies. It also runs a CDMO business providing end-to-end development and manufacturing services to pharmaceutical innovators and specialty companies, with products marketed in more than 150 countries.

outlook.body: Companion animal formulations (global market tailwinds); CDMO revenue ramp from FY28 (15+ high-value products); vertical integration of 7+ key products into API; expansion into LatAm and Europe via Turkey site; potential in-licensing of animal health products
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Three clear growth priorities: (1) build a leading Companion Animal health franchise through a focused product pipeline, strategic partnerships and deeper commercial presence in India and Europe; (2) grow the CDMO platform on high-value, complex-chemistry opportunities with long-term innovator partnerships; (3) geographically extend the existing formulations portfolio into new markets using the regulated manufacturing base and market-specific registrations
- R&D remains the core differentiator under the unified 'One R&D' framework; FY27 focus sharpens on companion animal products, oncology formulations and differentiated APIs
- Evaluating selective inorganic opportunities alongside organic scale-up given a significantly deleveraged balance sheet
- Human Health Formulations: scale the mature portfolio via India-based manufacturing, expand complex generics including an integrated oncology portfolio, and deepen presence in regulated markets
- Animal Health: strengthen Companion Animal position via strategic partnerships, portfolio expansion and selective M&A in key companion animal markets; for Farm Animals, pursue geographic expansion, address portfolio gaps and launch differentiated products
- CDMO growth strategy centred on targeted expansion in high-value opportunities, advancing early-stage molecules to commercial scale, optimising existing capacity, and partnership-led growth with innovators
- Continue pursuing procurement, manufacturing, R&D and commercial synergies from the SeQuent-Viyash integration
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Viyash Scientific operates 16 manufacturing facilities (10 API plants, 6 formulation plants) across India, Spain, Turkey, Brazil and the USA, following the FY26 Composite Scheme of Amalgamation that merged the Company with Symed Labs Limited, Vandana Life Sciences Private Limited, Appcure Labs Private Limited, Vindhya Pharma (India) Private Limited, S.V. Labs Private Limited, Vindhya Organics Private Limited, Viyash Life Sciences Private Limited, Geninn Life Sciences Private Limited and Sequent Research Limited (NCLT Hyderabad order dated November 18, 2025; effective December 16, 2025; appointed date April 1, 2025). During FY26 the Company received EU GMP approval for its Spanish manufacturing plant, set up a new injectable-focused R&D centre at Ankara University (Turkey) for the Alivira global animal-health business, and accelerated relocation of large-volume Human Health product manufacturing to India to improve cost competitiveness. It also expanded its India commercial field force by ~40 individuals and entered the Indian companion-animal market via a strategic distribution partnership with Boehringer Ingelheim India. Approximately 85% of key Human Health products are backward integrated. Forward-looking growth strategies name targeted expansion in high-value CDMO opportunities, capacity optimisation of existing infrastructure, and selective M&A in key companion-animal markets, without disclosed rupee capex quantum for any specific project.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Geoeconomic fragmentation and 'China+1' sourcing strategies are restructuring pharma/API supply chains, a structural tailwind for the sector
- Long-term demand supported by affordable generics, ageing populations, wider healthcare access, animal protein consumption and pet humanisation
- API manufacturers with diversified, reliable and cost-effective supply capabilities are expected to benefit as supply chains prioritise resilience
- Generic penetration in companion animals is below 15% versus ~70% in farm animals and ~91% in human health, representing a substantial untapped white space
- More than 190 molecules, including 60+ blockbusters, are expected to lose patent protection between 2025 and 2030, creating a genericisation opportunity
- Pharmaceutical companies increasingly rely on CDMOs for flexibility, scalability and cost efficiency, elevating outsourcing as a strategic growth channel
- Company's manufacturing presence in the United States and India supports proximity and responsiveness to large pharmaceutical markets
- Company positioned to benefit from India's rising relevance as an alternative sourcing destination given its 10 manufacturing plants and cost competitiveness
- API business: 19 items in R&D pipeline, 21 regulatory approvals and 19 product launches during FY26
- Human Health Formulations: 24+ finished dosage products currently under active development/pipeline, with 11 products carrying early launch opportunities, across 30+ commercial products in 7 categories
- API CDMO platform: 15 projects for innovator lifecycle management and 28 specialty generics projects across co-investment and CDMO models

deepdive.thesis: The NCLT-approved merger of SeQuent and Viyash has created an integrated life sciences player with immediate margin expansion (22% EBITDA) and a clear path to 20%+ sustainable margins, driven by synergies in R&D, manufacturing, and CDMO; what matters is the acceleration of companion animal formulations and API verticalization, positioning the combined entity as a global low-cost innovator in animal health.

open.item: Zoetis discontinued product (~INR12-14cr) expected to relaunch/return in FY26.
US FDA formulation project remains on hold; no acceleration expected in next 12-24 months.
Key focus on improving EBITDA-to-PAT conversion (Q4 EBITDA INR200cr vs PAT INR60cr) via lower finance cost and tax optimisation; further debt reduction.
Geopolitical raw-material/solvent/freight pressure since March 2026 (INR1-2cr Q4 freight hit); managed via inventory and price increases, no material impact expected near term.
In FY27, R&D will remain a priority investment area, with sharper focus on companion animal products, oncology formulations and differentiated APIs.
Goodwill/intangible amortisation (~INR100cr in FY26) drops to ~INR35cr in FY27, reducing the drag by ~INR65cr annually.
Investing in Spain manufacturing expansion, Turkey capacity debottlenecking, an oncology potent R&D lab (ready this/next quarter), and India companion-animal manufacturing.
FY27 is companion-animal platform-building: R&D expansion (5-6x product development, 7-8 products/year), manufacturing infrastructure, and BI distribution; first-phase Europe + India.
API to return to double-digit growth next year (FY27) as intermediate optimisation ends and approvals/animal-health APIs ramp.
Innovator/life-cycle-management (CDMO) business (~INR200-225cr base) expected to grow ~40% in FY27.
Synergies tracking ~INR50-60cr annualized; total expected to rise to ~INR125-150cr annualized over next 12-18 months.
US formulation (Appco, 60% owned, ~INR400-425cr rev) and Spain (60% owned, ~INR550cr rev) minorities (~20% of PAT); Spain buyback option by ~2028, being evaluated over next 1-2 years.
Effective tax rate expected ~26-27% for FY27/FY28 (post shift from old to new tax regime).
Targeting ~INR1,000cr EBITDA (from INR700cr) over next ~2-3 years, with ~15% annual growth guidance.
Gross margin (~54-55%) expected to be maintained, with only +/-1-2% variation over next few years.
~15% (up to 15-20%) revenue growth considered achievable over next 5 years across formulation, API and CDMO; detailed strategy at a planned investor meet.
Explore selective M&A opportunities in key companion animal markets.
Accelerating relocation of large-volume Human Health product manufacturing to India to improve cost competitiveness.
Evaluating selective inorganic opportunities alongside organic scale-up, supported by a significantly deleveraged balance sheet.
Deepen CDMO relationships with global innovators across human and animal health, focused on high-value, complex-chemistry opportunities.
